messages:
ava: quick postmortem from today's eu->us simulated cutover. saw latency tail and a legal question re: derived state crossing borders.

priya: can you summarize what "derived" means here? some cache entries are literally hashed handles, others have small user metadata.

ava: yes mixed bag. example: model prefix cache contains user name tokens in some cases. we also store request-level context blobs (they're marked as ephemeral but not redacted).

lee: fundamental question: do we allow any derived user data to leave residency? if not, fallback must avoid transferring those entries. that likely means cold miss and worse latency.

tom: tradeoff thought: allow metadata-only replication where we replace PII fields with salted hashes that are irreversible by default. then remote region can serve with lower latency but without reconstructing raw PII.

priya: legal will probably balk at irreversible transforms unless we can prove no re-identification path. need DPA sign-off. also auditing must show which tenants opted in.

ava: implementation sketch: 1) add residency_level enum on tenant: STRICT | TRANSFORM_ALLOWED | OPEN. 2) on write, attach residency_level and a pii_mask_version. 3) replication pipeline consults residency_level; if TRANSFORM_ALLOWED, run mask service to strip PII and write replicable cache.

lee: question: how expensive is masking at write time? microbench showed masking median 0.7ms, p95 2.2ms. acceptable for most tenants but affects high-throughput use.

tom: alternative is async mask during background replication. primary writes fast, replication process pulls unmasked entry from primary secured stream, masks, then pushes to other region. requires secure transfer and short-lived buffer in transit.

priya: that still transfers derived user data across network even if briefly. legal prefers local-only masking with no raw copy leaving the residency region. so masking at write time might be necessary for TRANSFORM_ALLOWED.

ava: we also discussed a metadata-only failover mode: remote region receives only non-user context (model config + anonymized prefix stats) and responds with a degraded response that asks the client to re-supply sensitive fields or switch to hosted EU fallback. That keeps guarantees tight.

lee: could combine modes: STRICT -> remote returns 403-ish fallback or proxy to EU control-plane; TRANSFORM_ALLOWED -> masked replication; OPEN -> full replication. map these to SLA tiers.

ops-bot: note: replication pipeline requires KMS policy update to allow masking service to read encryption context for TRANSFORM_ALLOWED tenants.

priya: product note: we need a console toggle per tenant and a billing flag if we provide active warm failover. customers must sign the cross-region replication clause.

tom: on the runtime side, to reduce cold-start, we can prewarm model kernels and warm generic KV namespaces (global templates) but never warm tenant-resident namespaces unless tenant allows transform or open. so warm-model + cold-tenant-data combo.

ava: that was effective in the spike: prewarm reduced model-init component of p95 by ~450ms. remaining is kv miss.

lee: for kv miss we can implement selective top-N warm: maintain access counters (only counts, no PII) and replicate LRU top items after masking. this obeys transform boundaries and limits bandwidth.

priya: auditing: any replicated entry must carry an audit token and replication event id, surfaced in tenant logs. legal wants review endpoint to list replicated keys and their mask_version.

ava: ops implications: need a reconciliation job to delete replicated masked entries after failback or when tenant revokes transform permission. must be idempotent and slow-delete safe.

tom: one more failure mode: what if mask_version evolves and old masked entries exist? plan: include mask_version in cache key namespace, and run a migration that recomputes masked entries lazily on access. keep old masked copies for a TTL.

lee: rolling this out: proposal: pilot with 3 consenting enterprise tenants on TRANSFORM_ALLOWED; run canary for 2 weeks, collect latency, correctness, and legal signoff.

priya: +1. i'll prep contract snippets and an internal checklist for DPA/KMS updates.

ava: action items: (1) add residency_level + mask_version to tenant schema (tom), (2) implement mask service and attach to write path with config toggle (lee + tom), (3) build audit log and replication event API (ava), (4) update failover runbook to support metadata-only degraded responses and legal checklist (priya), (5) run canary and 5 simulated failovers (ops).

ops-bot: created INFRA-2109 "residency-level cache strategy + masking pipeline" assigned to tom/lee. Link: https://issues.redwood/internal/INFRA-2109

ava: thanks team. let's review results in next ARCH sync.
